title: Kimi K3.1 Pro releases its weights, with datacenter serving and custom license limits
summary: The promised K3.1 Pro checkpoint is now publicly listed. Its 2.8T total parameters, model-specific deployment recipes and custom commercial terms make self-hosting a different decision from trying the paid API.

sections.title: The promised checkpoint is now visible
sections.html:
Kimi K3.1 Pro now has a publicly accessible weight repository. On November 8, 2026, the Hugging Face file listing exposed all 96 numbered safetensors shards, a model README, configuration and license; the listing reports 1.56 TB. This materially changes the October 24 assessment, when the launch article only promised weights by November 4. Repository commit dates do not establish when files first became publicly downloadable, so the exact public-release timestamp remains unconfirmed.

The versioned model README describes a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 2.8T total parameters, 104B activated parameters and a 1,048,576-token context. It lists MXFP4 weights and MXFP8 activations with quantization-aware training. Activated parameters describe computation per token, not the weight storage a deployment must accommodate. Neither that number nor the checkpoint size establishes total runtime memory.

The hosted Pro and Highspeed routes remain documented through Kimi products and API. The weight release adds inspectability and an infrastructure-controlled option; it does not demonstrate affordable laptop deployment, universal account access or parity between every hosted and self-hosted configuration.

sections.title: Self-hosting requires a specific serving configuration
sections.html:
The README links dedicated vLLM, SGLang and TokenSpeed recipes. This assessment inspected the first two. The vLLM recipe describes a basic NVIDIA setup using eight GPUs across two GB300 trays or one B300 node, and an MI355X path. These are documented configurations, not measured minimum requirements. The author says the baseline throughput was not tuned. Generic hub installation snippets omit consequential hardware, parser and parallelism settings.

Support also varies within one runtime. The vLLM page says its TPU path is text-only, does not load the vision tower, and currently requires a staging branch because support remains under review; no published image or wheel carries that path yet. Its Rubin preview has not been verified on Rubin. A version badge therefore cannot certify every hardware option underneath it.

The SGLang cookbook distinguishes verified combinations from recipes awaiting final-weight measurement and unverified playground settings. Its agentic long-context campaign records custom images, patches and measured versus derived router and cache choices. Those boundaries matter more than an isolated throughput number. A deployment evaluation should pin the actual recipe, image, checkpoint and parsers, then test tool calls, image handling, concurrent sessions and recovery under its own workload. No checkpoint download, installation or inference run was performed here.

sections.title: Read the custom license before choosing a distribution model
sections.html:
The Kimi K3.1-Pro license at the inspected revision grants broad use, modification, deployment and redistribution rights subject to conditions. It is a custom license, rather than an unrestricted MIT or Apache release. Copyright and permission notices must accompany copies, and use must comply with applicable laws.

Section 2 requires a separate Moonshot agreement before any commercial use when the licensee or any affiliate operates a Model as a Service business and their aggregate revenue exceeds US$20 million over any consecutive twelve months. Its service definition concerns third-party inference or fine-tuning access with meaningful control of inputs, parameters or training data. It excludes capabilities embedded solely in specific product features or harnesses, and mere relaying to models hosted elsewhere. The trigger considers affiliates and aggregate revenue; it is not simply a threshold on one endpoint's revenue.

Section 3 separately requires prominent Kimi K3.1-Pro branding for a commercial product or service above 100 million monthly active users or US$20 million monthly revenue. Sections 2 and 3 exempt internal use and access through official Moonshot products or certified inference partners. The internal-use definition excludes making the software, its outputs or underlying capabilities available to third parties. These distinct thresholds and exemptions should be mapped to the intended deployment; publishing weights does not remove them.

sections.title: The interesting creative claim is tool-directed construction
sections.html:
The launch article emphasizes work across game engines, interactive web scenes and parametric 3D modeling. It describes scripts for Blender and CAD software, adjustments to geometry and materials, and examples intended for games, brand films and websites. This is a model-and-tools workflow: the language model proposes or edits executable descriptions and uses an environment capable of building the result. It is not evidence that a bare text API response automatically contains a finished scene, functioning game or rendered video.

Kimi also says its 3D Make product can preview and edit models online and export forms suitable for printing, videos or Live Photos. That is a documented product pathway worth inspecting separately. This research did not enter the application, verify export formats, inspect geometry, test printability or watch rendered examples frame by frame. A creator should distinguish the provider’s demonstration of a workflow from the reliability of that workflow on an unfamiliar brief with specific dimensions, materials and output requirements.

An educational pilot could ask the model to produce a parameterized mechanical teaching model or an interactive geometry scene, then have learners inspect the parameters and explain how each changes the result. A game prototype might generate a small environment and a single interaction, with explicit checks for collisions, camera behavior and asset licenses. These are proposed uses grounded in the documented workflow, not measured educational outcomes or production-ready templates. The value would be making editable construction steps visible, followed by human inspection of the artifact.

sections.title: Access and prerequisites are specific
sections.html:
The K3.1 API guide says the flagship unlocks after a successful top-up of at least $1. Cumulative top-ups determine account tiers and rate limits. API access therefore requires an account, a key and paid credit, even if the first experiment is small. The general quickstart documents direct HTTP calls and compatibility with OpenAI or Anthropic API formats. Its examples require Python 3.9 or later, or Node.js 18 or later, and the relevant SDK. These are documented routes, not libraries installed or requests executed during this assessment.

The launch article says Kimi Work needs version 3.1.0 or later on Windows or Apple silicon Macs. Kimi Code users select the model through its model command. Enterprise administrators must explicitly enable it, with organization access off by default at launch. Product subscriptions and the pay-as-you-go API are distinct offerings; availability through a named application does not establish that an existing subscription includes unlimited use. Subscription prices, regional eligibility and detailed rate limits were not verified for this report.

A web application should keep the provider key on its server and pass only the data needed for the chosen task. A small coding pilot can instead use an existing supported agent client, but permissions and execution tools remain the client’s responsibility. Compatibility with an API format lowers integration effort; it does not certify every endpoint, option or error-handling behavior of a client built for another provider. The general quickstart is a starting point for that compatibility check.

sections.title: Highspeed costs more on some token categories
sections.html:
The November 8 official pricing table lists Pro at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Highspeed is $4 and $20 respectively. Both list cached input at $0.20 per million tokens. Highspeed therefore doubles the base input and output rates, but saying it simply doubles every bill would be inaccurate: repeated cached input has the same listed rate. The mix of reasoning, output, input, cache hits and additional tools determines the actual workload cost.

Caching is automatic for eligible repeated prefixes, with a default five-minute lifetime and an optional one-hour tier. The table separately lists five-minute cache writes at $2 per million for Pro and $4 for Highspeed; one-hour writes are $4 and $8. The billing explanation says writes are charged separately and cache hits incur no additional write charge. Partial blocks that do not fill a cache block are treated as misses according to the guide. An experiment should therefore inspect reported usage rather than estimate savings solely from repeated text.

Prices exclude applicable taxes. The API is described as pay-as-you-go without a subscription plan and is billed separately from Kimi memberships and Code. A million-token capacity is not a recommendation to resend a million tokens on each request. Begin with a small representative input, set an output budget appropriate to the task and record the successful task’s total cost, including retries. No paid calls, cache-hit measurements or invoices were produced for this report, and no claim of cost savings over another service is made.

sections.title: Several defaults can change the experience
sections.html:
The guide says thinking is always enabled and exposes low, high and max reasoning effort, with max as the default. It also fixes sampling settings rather than allowing arbitrary temperature or top-p choices. A ported client that sends familiar optional fields may therefore require changes. The documented default maximum completion allocation is 131,072 tokens and can be raised substantially; a builder should select a deliberate budget instead of inheriting a large value for a simple classroom interaction.

For multi-turn conversations and tool calls, the complete assistant message must be returned to the next request rather than retaining only the final text. Streaming separates reasoning and answer deltas, and strict structured output applies to the final content field. These details matter for an application that expects a typed answer, a tool argument or an editable script. A model can produce syntactically constrained data while still choosing wrong values; schema validation is useful but should be followed by task-specific checks.

Vision inputs require an array of content objects, and the guide specifically says public image URLs are unsupported: it documents base64 data or uploaded-file identifiers. This differs from some superficially similar APIs. The guide also warns that its official web-search tool is being updated and is not recommended for production workflows in the near term. A demonstration that relies on current sources therefore needs a separately verified retrieval path, or a fixed source pack supplied to the model. The availability of a tool name is not evidence that the entire research workflow is ready.

sections.title: Read the performance claims with their methodology
sections.html:
Moonshot claims a two-to-threefold speed increase for Highspeed. This remains a provider claim; no controlled latency test was performed here. Faster token production may shorten part of a task while leaving tool execution, rendering, network delay and retries untouched. For a creative builder, the useful comparison is time to an acceptable verified artifact under the same brief and budget.

The launch reports strong benchmark results with methodological footnotes covering different agent harnesses, selected task subsets, external scores and internal evaluations. Its CAD comparison uses a sampled subset for open models and certain scores from other providers' reports. This disclosure does not make every number an identical-condition contest. This assessment has not reproduced those benchmarks and does not rank the model from them.

The earlier October 24 inspection recorded placeholder benchmark values and inconsistent internal hallucination figures in the API guide. On November 8, the inspected guide no longer showed those placeholders and its described hallucination figures agreed with the launch article. That is a documentation correction, not independent validation of factual accuracy. The internal stress test still cannot be read as an everyday error probability. The checkpoint's availability and deployment documentation are now established documentary facts; quality, operational reliability and cost remain workload-dependent evaluation questions.

sections.title: Three bounded projects worth evaluating
sections.html:
A teaching prototype could generate an interactive web explanation of a physical system from a short specification and a few diagrams. Give it a fixed set of equations, insist that the interface expose assumptions, and test several known cases before showing it to learners. Record whether it produces a runnable project, whether the mathematics survives interaction and how much instructor editing is required. This evaluates a concrete instructional artifact; it does not let a visually convincing simulation certify its own scientific correctness.

An app or website experiment could supply a small existing codebase and ask for one feature with acceptance criteria: a responsive editor, a data visualization or an accessible settings panel. Compare Pro and Highspeed using the same source revision and tasks. Measure completed requirements, regressions, total elapsed time and billed usage. The long context may help keep relevant files available, but it does not eliminate the need to run tests, inspect changes and constrain tools. Larger context capacity alone is not evidence of reliable retrieval across every position.

For video work, a useful pilot is one editable Blender scene with a parameterized object, camera movement and lighting setup. Render a short preview with the actual production tools, check geometry and timing, and revise before attempting a longer sequence. Kimi’s stated capability is relevant to generating the construction scripts and assets; the renderer, compositing and final audio workflow remain separate. No end-to-end video production, export or asset-rights verification was performed for this report.

sections.title: What would change the assessment
sections.html:
The weight release changes the available choices. Builders can continue a bounded hosted pilot, while infrastructure teams can inspect the checkpoint, license and runtime-specific recipes before evaluating self-hosting. The substantial storage footprint and partially verified serving matrix make the latter an engineering project. A small institution need not operate this model merely to test its creative workflows.

The next useful evidence is a reproducible task comparison with usage records and inspected artifacts. Evaluate completed requirements, failure recovery and total cost, including retries and operational work. The report makes no assurance of self-hosting savings, unrestricted commercial licensing, improved learning or reliable autonomous delivery. Its practical recommendation is to match the access route to the task and require checkable outputs before expanding the pilot.

useCases: Evaluate a hosted coding model on a bounded web or app feature with explicit acceptance tests.
Create editable parametric 3D teaching assets or game prototypes, then inspect them in the target tool.
Generate and revise a short scripted Blender scene for a separately rendered video.
limitations: Public weight files and the versioned README/license were inspected; no weights were downloaded or executed. The exact first public-release timestamp remains unknown.
The 2.8T total / 104B activated model has a 1.56 TB listed repository. Active parameters and file size do not establish runtime memory or a minimum hardware configuration.
The custom license has distinct MaaS/affiliate-revenue and product-branding conditions, with specifically defined exemptions; it is not an unrestricted MIT or Apache release.
vLLM and SGLang recipes disclose hardware-specific staging, custom-image and verification limits. Documentation is not this project’s deployment test.

Provider speed, benchmark and quality claims were not independently tested. The earlier API documentation inconsistencies were corrected in the November 8 pages, without validating the underlying benchmarks.
Official web search remains documented as unsuitable for current production workflows. API top-up, separate cache-write billing and unverified subscription/regional entitlement remain relevant.

judgment: Public weights make K3.1 Pro inspectable and self-hostable in principle, with substantial infrastructure requirements and custom license conditions. The hosted API remains the simpler bounded pilot; either route needs output, usage and reliability checks.
researchNote: Original October 24 assessment revised after November 8 Chrome inspection of the full weight-file listing, versioned README and license at d9e99b0792a5e93b78ea9bea62a68167e36ddd9e, model-specific vLLM/SGLang recipes and current primary API documentation. The standalone model landing page failed after one repair; the linked versioned README was separately inspected successfully. No account, top-up, API call, software installation, full checkpoint download or generated-artifact test. Original discovery date and section anchors preserved; exact original publication and first public-weight-release dates remain unknown.
